recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should continue refining source/signatures.html or Provenance-based examples if needed, but should not revive Bundle.signature-specific usage guidance unless the work group reverses the later deprecation decision.
issue_request: FHIR-7693 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It requested rationale for Bundle signatures on documents, messages, transactions, and query responses; a usage note that signing, verification, and unsigned-bundle handling are implementation-environment specific; and a datatype change from base64Binary to Signature.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in svn revision 5820, now git commit 2e87ff782b75b5c2f1945c9e475fc1057a4056d1, by adding the requested rationale and usage note to the historical Bundle spreadsheet source. That content was carried into the current StructureDefinition source until the later digital-signature rewrite.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml keeps Bundle.signature as a 0..1 Signature element but marks it deprecated and points to Provenance-based signatures. Later FHIR-51099 and FHIR-I minutes decided not to relax Bundle.signature cardinality because the preferred approach is Bundle.entry Provenance signatures, and FHIR-52810 has already updated the embedded Bundle signature target rule on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Re-adding the exact 2015 rationale to the deprecated Bundle.signature element would conflict with the current Provenance/deprecation direction; the current signatures page already covers authenticity, integrity, non-repudiation, local policy for signing and verification, and Bundle signing via Provenance.
